title: Awards, polls and critics matter less over time
summary: Herman says awards and reviews matter less the longer you live.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: You know, thinking about that, I know you must have opinions about awards and polls and things, and you've gone through that through your whole career.
What value do you place on it, plus or minus, or does it do anything?

-- for the moment, I think anyone is quite thrilled and pleased with the fact that you're receiving some adulation, by some crook of fate. But I think the longer you live, the less dent it makes on your whole thinking pattern, because they're just simply awards and so on. And a critique or a critique takes on less and less value, because everything that's said about you has been said before, and this is just another occasion.
And you read it because you're supposed to, but not because it influences you one way or the other, or makes any big color in your life.
